question:
A 25-year-old female presents with a three-month history of severe pulsating headaches, rating 8/10 in
intensity. She has made two emergency department visits in the past month for headaches, with
elevated blood pressure noted during both visits. Her medical history includes polycystic ovarian
disease, and she takes metformin and oral contraceptives. Physical examination reveals: - Height: 162
cm, Weight: 86 kg, BMI: 33 kg/m2 - Temperature: 37.0°C, Pulse: 99/min, Blood pressure: 168/98 mm
Hg - Hirsutism present - Normal cardiopulmonary findings - Soft, nontender abdomen with left-sided
abdominal bruit - No focal neurological findings Laboratory results show normal complete blood count,
electrolytes, urea nitrogen, creatinine, and plasma free metanephrines. Imaging studies reveal: -
Abdominal ultrasound: Increased peak systolic velocity in left distal renal artery - CT angiography:
8-mm distal segment of left renal artery showing alternating stenosis and dilation with ~75% diameter
reduction; left kidney significantly smaller than right - Brain CT: Normal What is the most appropriate
next step in management? Answer Choices: (A) Conservative management with lifestyle modifications
and weight loss (B) Surgical nephrectomy of the affected kidney (C) Ramipril and percutaneous
transluminal angioplasty without stent placement (D) Discontinuation of oral contraceptive and initiation
of beta-blocker therapy (E) Renal artery embolization (F) Surgical revascularization with bypass
grafting (G) Percutaneous transluminal angioplasty with stent placement (H) Combination therapy with

losartan and spironolactone (I) Medical management with amlodipine and hydrochlorothiazide (J)
Combination therapy with captopril and valsartan
 A. Surgical nephrectomy of the affected kidney
B. Medical management with amlodipine and hydrochlorothiazide
C. Conservative management with lifestyle modifications and weight loss
D. Ramipril and percutaneous transluminal angioplasty without stent placement
E. Percutaneous transluminal angioplasty with stent placement
F. Surgical revascularization with bypass grafting
G. Discontinuation of oral contraceptive and initiation of beta-blocker therapy
H. Combination therapy with losartan and spironolactone
I. Renal artery embolization
J. Combination therapy with captopril and valsartan
